subject: zone_catalog
claim: In the r806919.Wizard_1_610 install used here, which holds 3,599 GameData archives, the zone data defines 3,366 zones; each zone's id is the KI string hash of its path and is unique, its gamedata.bin is in the archive named by the path with / replaced by - and .wad appended, and its first path component is its world namespace.
how_to_repeat: Read Bin/revision.dat from your own install and confirm it reports r806919.Wizard_1_610.
Run the built extractor with --client <your install> --type-dump <your matching type dump> --dry-run zones and record its zone-template and archive counts.
Run contrib/tools/ambrose-zone-catalog/catalog.py with the same install, matching type dump and built extractor, using --json to print the catalog.
Confirm the JSON catalog has one unique id per zone, and decode Root.wad's WorldHubZones.xml with bindecode to compare the mapped m_world values with the zone-path namespaces.
Use client types WizZoneData to inspect its properties and confirm whether it carries a separate m_world field.
evidence: The extractor reported 3,366 zone_template rows from 3,599 archives, 9,874 locations, 67,386 decoded objects and no extraction errors; its dry run wrote nothing.
The JSON catalog for this install contains 3,366 unique zone paths. The KI string hashes of those paths were unique; the Commons and Ravenwood hashes were 1727411499 and 699201167, respectively.
A second r806919 install produced 3,356 zones from 3,589 archives, so these totals describe the install used here rather than every install of this revision.
ZoneExtractor checks that each zone path, with slashes replaced by hyphens, matches the GameData archive stem; ZoneExtractorClientTest.EveryZoneArchiveReadsAndNoTwoZonesSharePath passed.
The zone paths had 113 distinct first-component namespaces. WorldHubZones.xml carried 117 hub mappings across 114 distinct m_world names; two zone namespaces were not in that hub-world set.
The type dump lists m_zoneName on WizZoneData and does not list an m_world property.

A second observation, on the reference r806919.Wizard_1_610 install, whose Data/GameData holds 3,589 archives: its extractor reported 3,356 zone_template rows, 9,861 locations and 67,325 objects with no extraction error, and catalog.py --json printed 3,356 zones, every one of which matches this list on path, id, world and archive.

The ten zones this list holds beyond the reference install's are exactly the zones of the ten archives that install lacks, Avalon-Interiors-AV_Z03_EstateFroudling.wad, DragonSpire-DS_A1_Knowledge-Interiors-DS_GrandChasm_T4.wad, Empyrea-Interiors-EM_Z04_FireDwarfHouse.wad, MooShu-MS_War-Interiors-MS_War2_T4.wad and WizardCity-WC_Streets-Interiors-WC_Colossus_CE_T1_L1.wad to L6.wad, which contrib/findings/data/kiwad_archive_inventory.json names; no other zone differs between the two installs.
disproof: A repeat on r806919 that finds a duplicate zone hash, a zone path whose archive stem differs, an extractor error, or client data showing that a zone's first path component is not its world namespace would disprove this catalog.
scope_note: The zone id, path, namespace and zone-data archive are names and ids, not client content. The archive field names the GameData WAD containing gamedata.bin, not every asset WAD the zone may reference; the companion finding records the other archives that hold placed-object templates. The world field is the data's path namespace; WizZoneData has no separate world property, and the hub map does not explicitly associate every namespace.
